readmeExcerpt:
The model can be anyone's. The agent should be yours.

Codewhale is an open-source coding agent for your terminal, written in Rust. It works with any model, can split one task across several agents, and every line of it is yours to read. ```bash curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh ``` This installs the latest release on macOS or Linux, and it needs no account. [Windows, npm and Cargo](#install) are below. [Website](https://codewhale.net) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) [简体中文](docs/i18n/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/i18n/README.ja-JP.md) · [Tiếng Việt](docs/i18n/README.vi.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](docs/i18n/README.id.md) · [한국어](docs/i18n/README.ko-KR.md) · [Español](docs/i18n/README.es-419.md) · [Português](docs/i18n/README.pt-BR.md) · [Русский](docs/i18n/README.ru.md) · [Українська](docs/i18n/README.uk.md) · [Français](docs/i18n/README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](docs/i18n/README.de.md) · [繁體中文](docs/i18n/README.zh-TW.md) · [हिन्दी](docs/i18n/README.hi.md) · [Türkçe](docs/i18n/README.tr.md) · [Italiano](docs/i18n/README.it.md) · [Polski](docs/i18n/README.pl.md) · [العربية](docs/i18n/README.ar.md) · [Català](docs/i18n/README.ca.md) A real session on a 0.10.3 development build: deepseek-flash through DeepSeek's API wrote the edit, and you allowed the test run once.
## Install The command above puts checksum-verified `codewhale` and its short alias `codew` in `~/.local/bin`. If your shell then says `command not found`, follow the PATH note the installer prints ([details](docs/INSTALL.md#put-it-on-your-path)). `codewhale update` upgrades it. ```bash winget install --id HunterBown.CodeWhale --exact --source winget # Windows x64 npm install -g codewhale # wraps the same release binaries cargo install codewhale-cli --locked # builds from source; can trail GitHub Releases ``` Prebuilt binaries cover Linux, macOS and Windows on x64 and arm64. Scoop, Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android and Termux (preview) and manual downloads are in the [installation guide](docs/INSTALL.md), and containers are in [Docker](docs/DOCKER.md). Use one install method per machine; otherwise two copies end up on your `PATH` and whichever comes first wins. ## Quickstart 1. Commit or stash your work, then run `codewhale` from the root of a git repository. By default it applies file edits there without asking and asks before each shell command that is not read-only. 2. Run `/provider` (or press `F3`), pick a provider, paste its API key and choose a model. DeepSeek is the default provider. On a first launch with no key, Codewhale asks for a provider when you send your first message, and it offers a local model when a local Ollama server answers. 3. Type a task: ```text Fix the failing tests and explain what changed. ``` Read-only commands run straight away. For any other shell command Codewhale asks first: `y` runs it once, `a` allows commands like it for the rest of the conversation, and `n` refuses. `/undo` takes back your last request and its file changes, and `/help` lists commands and keys. For scripts and CI, `codewhale exec` runs one task without the interface. Read [headless runs](docs/INSTALL.md#headless-scripts-ci) before you give it tools with `--auto`, because `--auto` uses Full Access unless you add a sandbox. ## What it does Give Codewhale a task and it reads the repository, edits files and runs commands until the task is done or it needs your input. The [latest release notes](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/releases/latest) list the newest changes, and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) has every version. ### Any model More than 40 providers are built in, including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter and xAI. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and so do local models through Ollama, vLLM or SGLang. The default model is DeepSeek's `deepseek-flash`, which now serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ([details](docs/PROVIDERS.md#deepseek-v41-flash)). `/model` switches models between turns, and `/model auto` picks one for each turn (`/router` sets up how). `/turn inspect` shows which model a turn used, what it cost and how long it took. See [Providers](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Receipts and undo `/receipts`, or `codewhale receipts --last` after you quit, lists the files a session changed, the commands it ran, its web and MCP calls, the agents it started, each approval and who gave it, and what failed. `/undo` takes back your last request and the files it changed in one step. `/restore` rolls the whole workspace back to an earlier snapshot, and because that overwrites later edits it needs `/trust on` or Full Access. See [Receipts](docs/RECEIPTS.md). ### Several agents on one task `/goal` sets an objective that carries across turns. Codewhale can split work across [sub-agents](docs/SUBAGENTS.md), run a [Fleet](docs/FLEET.md) of agents with their own roles and models, or follow a [workflow](docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md) checked into the repository. ### Plugins Connect [MCP servers](docs/MCP.md), add [skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [plugins](docs/PLUGINS.md), and run [hooks](docs/HOOKS.md) on session and tool events. Code mode (experimental, on by default) lets the model write one `execute_tools` program that calls several MCP and plugin tools; each call still meets your approval rules and keeps its receipt. [Computer Use](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-cu-plugin) is a separate plugin released on its own (experimental, macOS only), and stays off until you review its access and turn it on. ### Ways to run it | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `codewhale` | The interactive terminal app | | `codewhale exec "…"` | One task without the interface, for scripts and CI ([headless runs](docs/INSTALL.md#headless-scripts-ci)) | | `codewhale web` | A local web client on `127.0.0.1` ([guide](docs/WEB.md)) | | `codewhale review --pr N` | An advisory review of a GitHub pull request; the [GitHub bot setup](docs/GITHUB_ACTION.md#set-up-your-own-bot) runs it on your own model key | | `codewhale app-server --http` | The [Runtime API](docs/RUNTIME_API.md), a local HTTP API for threads, events, approvals and each turn's file changes | | `codewhale serve --acp` | The Agent Client Protocol over stdio, for editors such as Zed | The terminal app, `exec`, `web` and the Runtime API share one engine ([architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). A community-maintained [VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=HengQuWorld.brotherwhale-vscode) connects to it from the sidebar ([source](https://github.com/HengQuWorld/CodeWhale-VSCode)).

Codewhale × OrcaRouter gives 30% extra DeepSeek V4.1 Flash credit on each OrcaRouter top-up until November 21, 2026. This link is part of a referral campaign; Codewhale may earn a referral reward on top-ups made through it. ## How it stays safe Two switches say how much Codewhale may do on its own. `Tab`, when the input is empty, changes the mode: **Plan** reads and searches but changes nothing, **Work** edits files and runs commands, and **Operate** has the same access as Work and keeps going until the goal is verified or it needs you. `Shift+Tab` changes the permission. **Ask**, the default, applies file edits in your repository without asking and asks before shell commands that are not read-only. **Auto-Review** lets rules and a reviewer model approve routine calls and refuses high-risk ones; switch to Ask to approve those yourself. **Full Access** never asks and turns off Codewhale's sandbox, although repository rules and managed policy still apply. The [v0.10.2 guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/v0.10.2/docs/MODES.md) has the details. Coming in 0.10.3: `Shift+Tab` becomes one dial through Ask, Accept Edits, Plan, Auto-Review and Full Access, `Tab` no longer changes the mode, and Operate is retired. Ask will ask before every file edit too, and the new default, Accept Edits, will apply edits inside the git repository and still ask before commands. The [current guide](docs/MODES.md) describes it. In Ask and Auto-Review, commands run in an OS sandbox where the system has one: Seatbelt on macOS, and bubblewrap on Linux when it is installed. Windows has no OS sandbox yet, and Full Access turns the sandbox off. Inside the sandbox, shell commands and terminal sessions cannot read credential stores such as `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws` and `.env` files. `/preview-request` shows a redacted preview of the next request without sending it. You need no account, and keys you add with `/provider` stay on your machine. With your own API key you pay the provider directly, and local models need no key. The footer and `/cost` show what a session has cost when the price is known, and an unknown price is shown as unknown, never as free. Telemetry is on by default. It sends aggregate counts (version and platform, session length and outcome, which built-in providers you used, feature and error counts) with a random install ID that rotates every 90 days, and never conversations, code, prompts, model names, file or repository names, or credentials. This command turns it off: ```bash codewhale config set telemetry false ``` At startup Codewhale also checks GitHub for a new release; set `CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to skip that. More in [authorization order](docs/AUTHORIZATION_ORDER.md), [sandboxing](docs/SANDBOX.md) and [telemetry](docs/TELEMETRY.md). ## Where it is going Codewhale is becoming one environment across your terminal, a desktop app, the browser and cloud computers, all run by one engine. Each part says where it stands today. | Part | State | Today | | --- | --- | --- | | Terminal app | Released | Install it on macOS, Linux or Windows and run `codewhale` in any repository. | | Local browser client | Released | Run `codewhale web` to read the conversation, send a task and answer approvals in your browser; it comes with the terminal and needs no account. | | Many agents on one task | Released | Sub-agents, Fleets and workflows let several agents share one task, each with its own role. | | Desktop app | In development, no download | We are building a desktop app on the same engine, and it has no public download yet. | | Cloud computers | Invite-only | Cloud computers are invite-only, and we are building them so a session can keep working on a machine in the cloud. | | One session across them | Being built | We are building one session that goes with you from the terminal to the desktop, the browser and the cloud, and stays yours the whole way. | The [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) says what each release covers and where you can help. ## Coming from another agent Codewhale reads `AGENTS.md` on its own. Instruction files written for other tools, such as `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, load only when you opt in with `project_instruction_imports = ["claude"]` (or `"cursor"`, `"cline"`, `"windsurf"`, `"copilot"`, `"all"`) in your config; see [config.example.toml](config.exam

winget install --id HunterBown.CodeWhale --exact --source winget  # Windows x64

Scoop, Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android and Termux (preview) and manual downloads are in the installation guide, and containers are in Docker. Use one install method per machine; otherwise two copies end up on your PATH and whichever comes first wins.

Quickstart

  2. Run /provider (or press F3), pick a provider, paste its API key and choose a model. DeepSeek is the default provider. On a first launch with no key, Codewhale asks for a provider when you send your first message, and it offers a local model when a local Ollama server answers.
  3. Type a task:
Fix the failing tests and explain what changed.

For scripts and CI, codewhale exec runs one task without the interface. Read headless runs before you give it tools with --auto, because --auto uses Full Access unless you add a sandbox.

What it does

Give Codewhale a task and it reads the repository, edits files and runs commands until the task is done or it needs your input. The latest release notes list the newest changes, and the changelog has every version.

Any model

More than 40 providers are built in, including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter and xAI. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and so do local models through Ollama, vLLM or SGLang. The default model is DeepSeek's deepseek-flash, which now serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (details).

/model switches models between turns, and /model auto picks one for each turn (/router sets up how). /turn inspect shows which model a turn used, what it cost and how long it took. See Providers.

Receipts and undo

/receipts, or codewhale receipts --last after you quit, lists the files a session changed, the commands it ran, its web and MCP calls, the agents it started, each approval and who gave it, and what failed. /undo takes back your last request and the files it changed in one step. /restore rolls the whole workspace back to an earlier snapshot, and because that overwrites later edits it needs /trust on or Full Access. See Receipts.

Several agents on one task

/goal sets an objective that carries across turns. Codewhale can split work across sub-agents, run a Fleet of agents with their own roles and models, or follow a workflow checked into the repository.

Plugins

Connect MCP servers, add skills and plugins, and run hooks on session and tool events. Code mode (experimental, on by default) lets the model write one execute_tools program that calls several MCP and plugin tools; each call still meets your approval rules and keeps its receipt. Computer Use is a separate plugin released on its own (experimental, macOS only), and stays off until you review its access and turn it on.

Ways to run it

Command What it does
codewhale The interactive terminal app
codewhale exec "…" One task without the interface, for scripts and CI (headless runs)
codewhale web A local web client on 127.0.0.1 (guide)
codewhale review --pr N An advisory review of a GitHub pull request; the GitHub bot setup runs it on your own model key
codewhale app-server --http The Runtime API, a local HTTP API for threads, events, approvals and each turn's file changes
codewhale serve --acp The Agent Client Protocol over stdio, for editors such as Zed

The terminal app, exec, web and the Runtime API share one engine (architecture). A community-maintained VS Code extension connects to it from the sidebar (source).

How it stays safe

Two switches say how much Codewhale may do on its own. Tab, when the input is empty, changes the mode: Plan reads and searches but changes nothing, Work edits files and runs commands, and Operate has the same access as Work and keeps going until the goal is verified or it needs you. Shift+Tab changes the permission. Ask, the default, applies file edits in your repository without asking and asks before shell commands that are not read-only. Auto-Review lets rules and a reviewer model approve routine calls and refuses high-risk ones; switch to Ask to approve those yourself. Full Access never asks and turns off Codewhale's sandbox, although repository rules and managed policy still apply. The v0.10.2 guide has the details.

Coming in 0.10.3: Shift+Tab becomes one dial through Ask, Accept Edits, Plan, Auto-Review and Full Access, Tab no longer changes the mode, and Operate is retired. Ask will ask before every file edit too, and the new default, Accept Edits, will apply edits inside the git repository and still ask before commands. The current guide describes it.

In Ask and Auto-Review, commands run in an OS sandbox where the system has one: Seatbelt on macOS, and bubblewrap on Linux when it is installed. Windows has no OS sandbox yet, and Full Access turns the sandbox off. Inside the sandbox, shell commands and terminal sessions cannot read credential stores such as ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and .env files. /preview-request shows a redacted preview of the next request without sending it.

You need no account, and keys you add with /provider stay on your machine. With your own API key you pay the provider directly, and local models need no key. The footer and /cost show what a session has cost when the price is known, and an unknown price is shown as unknown, never as free.

Telemetry is on by default. It sends aggregate counts (version and platform, session length and outcome, which built-in providers you used, feature and error counts) with a random install ID that rotates every 90 days, and never conversations, code, prompts, model names, file or repository names, or credentials. This command turns it off:

codewhale config set telemetry false

At startup Codewhale also checks GitHub for a new release; set CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to skip that. More in authorization order, sandboxing and telemetry.

Where it is going

Codewhale is becoming one environment across your terminal, a desktop app, the browser and cloud computers, all run by one engine. Each part says where it stands today.

Part State Today
Terminal app Released Install it on macOS, Linux or Windows and run codewhale in any repository.
Local browser client Released Run codewhale web to read the conversation, send a task and answer approvals in your browser; it comes with the terminal and needs no account.
Many agents on one task Released Sub-agents, Fleets and workflows let several agents share one task, each with its own role.
Desktop app In development, no download We are building a desktop app on the same engine, and it has no public download yet.
Cloud computers Invite-only Cloud computers are invite-only, and we are building them so a session can keep working on a machine in the cloud.
One session across them Being built We are building one session that goes with you from the terminal to the desktop, the browser and the cloud, and stays yours the whole way.

The roadmap says what each release covers and where you can help.

Coming from another agent

Codewhale reads AGENTS.md on its own. Instruction files written for other tools, such as CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules or .github/copilot-instructions.md, load only when you opt in with project_instruction_imports = ["claude"] (or "cursor", "cline", "windsurf", "copilot", "all") in your config; see config.example.toml. Codewhale warns when it finds one it did not load.

/import-claude prepares an import of your Claude Code settings and MCP servers for you to review. /plugin install accepts Claude Code plugins that contain skills, commands, agent profiles and MCP servers, and refuses plugins that need hooks or LSP servers (details).

Documentation

These guides follow the main branch and can describe changes that are not in the latest release yet.

Start here Reference
User guide Configuration
Installation Architecture
Providers and local models Runtime API
Modes and permissions Plugin authoring
Keybindings Receipts
GitHub pull request review All documentation

Contributing

Codewhale is built in the open by the people who use it, in many languages.

The contributor wall counts everyone whose code, co-authored commits, carried-forward pull requests or credited reports are in Codewhale, including people GitHub's own contributor list misses. scripts/contributor-wall.py regenerates the picture and the list from git history and GitHub.

All feedback is welcome: a bug, an idea, or something that looked or felt wrong. Open an issue for any of these; an issue is also the best place to start a new feature. Pull requests are welcome for fixes, translations, providers and planned work. Questions go to Discussions. The contributing guide shows where each kind of help goes, how your work lands with your name on it, and where things live.

Chat on Discord, or add the maintainer, Hunter, on WeChat (hunterbown) and ask to join the Whale Brothers group. Everyone is welcome.

History and license

Codewhale started as deepseek-tui and still reads that project's configuration and sessions. It is independently maintained and not affiliated with DeepSeek or any other model provider.

MIT. Code adapted from other open-source projects is listed in the third-party notices for vendored sources and adapted designs.

releases.name: Codewhale v0.10.3
releases.body:
## What's in v0.10.3


Codewhale v0.10.3 brings a unified Plugins surface with Creator mode (`[features] plugin_creator`) and unmodified DeepSeek Harness (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`) plugin compatibility, an upgraded Auto-Review guardian with workspace boundaries, soft rules, sub-agent return review, and one-use retry approvals, and a single `Shift+Tab` permission dial defaulting to Accept Edits (`Ask → Accept Edits → Plan → Auto-Review → Full Access`). It moves the ACP server and external-agent sessions (including Qwen Code and GitHub Copilot CLI) onto the official Agent Client Protocol SDK, publishes native signed HarmonyOS ARM64 release assets, adds a verified signed model-and-provider registry channel alongside unified model-ID resolution and managed `/v1/models` pricing, updates design tokens to `5.4.0` with a docked single-line approval strip, folded turn activity, live working-row light sweeps and 13 hex-lattice dot-whale forms, adds `claude-org` billing auth, `show_data` transcript charts, `codewhale sessions migrate`, DeepSeek Chatbot web search and speech tools, receipted self-updates and `codewhale uninstall`, and lands reliability, CJK/Unicode, Windows, and sandbox security f

releases.name: Codewhale v0.10.2
releases.body:
## What's in v0.10.2


Codewhale v0.10.2 adds an animated pet view (`/pet on`), a live Terminal work
dock, per-chat composer colors (`/color`) and a one-time note on the first
start after an update that says what changed. It closes three session
data-loss paths and a `codewhale web` session leak; adds the default Runtime
daemon socket locations to the sandbox deny-list; holds a `curl` or `wget` that uploads a
credential; refuses shell commands containing invisible Unicode; keeps the
Linux sandbox working when a hidden credential directory is a symlink; and
reduces idle TUI redraw work. `/undo` takes back a whole
request, including long and multiline prompts. `exec --auto` explains its
Full Access default, honors an explicitly stricter sandbox, and saves
tool-enabled runs and their failure receipts. Local runtimes appear during
onboarding, `/diff` works outside a Git repository, DeepSeek's Responses route
no longer rejects replayed tool history, and contributor fixes improve token
accounting, relay model lists, localized replies and Windows launcher
guidance. Delegated work continues without model-invented turn or time caps,
and independent workflow steps can continue after another

releases.name: v0.10.1
releases.body:
> **Codewhale** is the public product from Shannon Labs. The `codewhale`
> command, npm package, and release-asset names remain lowercase technical
> identifiers. The legacy npm package `deepseek-tui` is deprecated and
> receives no further releases. Users coming from v0.8.x legacy `deepseek` /
> `deepseek-tui` names should migrate with `docs/REBRAND.md`.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.1" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source terminal coding agent that runs directly in your command line to modify codebases autonomously.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: CodeWhale is an interactive terminal coding agent designed to run seamlessly in the command line interface without managing heavy IDE extensions. It allows users to query and chat with LLMs while giving them the ability to natively run bash commands, read local files, write and edit code, and access tools over the internet via DuckDuckGo. The agent leverages Claude-3.5-Sonnet to orchestrate actions in an iterative feedback loop where it can read its environment, make changes, verify the outcome, and apply recursive solutions. The interface is highly optimized for terminal environments utilizing python-prompt-toolkit.
keyFeatures: Terminal execution loop: Executes natively in the terminal without requiring heavy web interfaces or editor plugins.
Autonomous shell commands: Has the ability to automatically execute bash scripts and shell commands to explore its environment.
File reading and writing: Natively accesses local filesystem files to implement and refine code blocks.
Web search integration: Incorporates search functions utilizing the DuckDuckGo API to research solutions and verify bugs online.
Local memory and config: Persists AI interactions and configurations gracefully within local storage for continuity.

useCases.title: Headless Server Maintenance
useCases.description: Administrators use the terminal agent over SSH sessions to parse confusing log files and suggest command line fixes.

useCases.title: Rapid Test Generation
useCases.description: Developers use the agent to write test cases and verify execution results iteratively without breaking terminal focus.

useCases.title: Unfamiliar Code Exploration
useCases.description: Engineers drop the agent into an unfamiliar directory structure and ask it to explain file connections or find specific logic.

useCases.title: Automated Debugging Workflows
useCases.description: Programmers allow the agent to repeatedly run compiler commands and autonomously read stack traces until it finds the root cause.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers and system administrators who require a fast, headless terminal coding agent capable of autonomously interacting with local files and bash sessions. They can query LLMs and natively execute shell commands to modify their codebases. It is ideal for iterative feedback loops during development.
